proposed_widenings.name: passive_grant (class-feature family)
proposed_widenings.justification: Fighting Style is a permanent passive benefit acquired at level 1. It has no activationCost, no use-count resource, and no rest-reset cadence. The existing activation family is intrinsically wrong for a once-granted passive feat slot. A new family (e.g. passive_grant) is required for class features whose entire mechanic is 'you gain X permanently at level N, with optional replacement rules.'
proposed_widenings.evidence: You have honed your martial prowess and gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see 'Feats').

proposed_widenings.name: grant_feat_choice (ClassFeatureEffect variant)
proposed_widenings.justification: The effect is granting access to a feat drawn from a named category (Fighting Style feats), with the player choosing which one. This is distinct from grant_extra_action or heal_hp. The closed category constraint and the player-choice semantics need a new effect variant.
proposed_widenings.evidence: gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see 'Feats')

proposed_widenings.name: replaceable_on_level_up (modifier on feat-choice effects)
proposed_widenings.justification: The feature explicitly permits swapping the chosen feat for a different one from the same category whenever the fighter gains a level. This is a character-progression mechanic with no analog in current atoms — it is not a rest-window reset nor an action-economy cost.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

notes: The individual Fighting Style feats (Defense, Archery, Great Weapon Fighting, Two-Weapon Fighting) carry the actual mechanical atoms — e.g. Defense grants +1 AC (modify_ac), Archery grants +2 to ranged attack rolls (modify_roll_numeric). The class feature itself is purely a feat-access grant. The activation family cannot honestly represent this unit because ClassFeatureMechanicsHeader requires resource (use_count) and resetCadence, neither of which exist here.
